title: SolveSpace NG review 1: menus
brief: Each menu, dark and light. For each: keep as is, tweak, or rethink, and a note. The questions say how Fusion 360, Onshape, FreeCAD, SOLIDWORKS and Blender arrange the same things. Concrete proposals are in round 3.

sheets.label: file
sheets.question: File. Others: Fusion, Onshape and FreeCAD group the many export formats under one Export submenu; Linux/macOS apps say Quit rather than Exit.

sheets.label: edit
sheets.question: Edit. Others: Configuration is 'Preferences' in Fusion, FreeCAD and Blender; view settings sit in View, not Edit.

sheets.label: view
sheets.question: View. Others: Blender and Fusion list their panels here with keys, and FreeCAD/SOLIDWORKS have a Standard Views submenu (Front, Top, Right, Isometric). NG panels (Outliner O, Properties N, Problems Shift+P), the theme and the numpad views are missing; 'Show Toolbar' now shows the tool shelf.

sheets.label: new group
sheets.question: New Group (Fusion's Create menu). Capitals are inconsistent: 'Sketch In 3d' (others write 3D). Lathe and Helix have no key.

sheets.label: sketch
sheets.question: Sketch. Others name tools briefly: Arc, Spline, Text (here 'Arc of a Circle', 'Bezier Cubic Spline', 'Text in TrueType Font').

sheets.label: constrain
sheets.question: Constrain. The Modern keys reach these through D (dimension) and F (constrain pie), so most show no key; 'Distance / Diameter' could at least show D.

sheets.label: analyze
sheets.question: Analyze (Fusion's Inspect). Matches what others offer; 'Step Dimension' is SolveSpace's own.

sheets.label: help
sheets.question: Help. Others add a keyboard shortcut list; NG could show the keymap here.
